findings.change_summary: No advancement found beyond proposed/permitting. Existing read-only Postgres timeline (fetch_timeline.py) shows only proposed/Feb-2024 and operating(planned)/2028 entries -- no FEED, EPC, permit, or construction milestone recorded. Web search (targeted queries for 2025/2026 construction start, groundbreaking, notice-to-proceed, ECC issuance, FEED) turned up no news of physical construction. The DENR/EMB environmental critical projects list as of 30 June 2025 does not show an issued ECC for the San Francisco Power Plant / QPPL project (fetch of the EMB PDF itself was blocked by Cloudflare, so this is corroborative, not primary, evidence). EGCO Group's July 2026 'POWER4' 2026 strategy press release discusses the existing 460 MW Quezon coal plant's new PSA but does not mention the LNG project at all, consistent with no material progress to report. DOE Luzon Indicative Power Projects listings (May 2023 through Nov 2025, per search snippets) continue to show the project at 1,200 MW with commercial operation year 2028 unchanged -- direct PDF fetch blocked by Cloudflare on both prod-cms.doe.gov.ph and legacy.doe.gov.ph, so not independently verified beyond search-result snippets. Net: status remains proposed; re-verified unchanged (blue).

Unchanged. Independent sources consistently report the 1,200 MW power-plant capacity and P71 billion (~US$1.2B) investment, but none state an LNG regasification/import mtpa figure for this specific facility, so the existing 1.1 mtpa GEM value could not be independently corroborated or contradicted via web search. No qa action taken since no conflicting value was found; noting in qa_notes for visibility.

Unchanged. Quezon Power (Philippines) Ltd Co remains 100% indirectly owned by Electricity Generating PCL (EGCO, Thailand) via its own investor-relations press release plus an independent news corroboration. A separate MGen (Meralco PowerGen)-EGCO joint venture (San Buenaventura Power Ltd) exists for an unrelated 460 MW coal plant -- confirmed this is NOT the same entity as QPPL/the Mauban LNG project, ruling out a false ownership-change lead surfaced mid-search.
Unchanged. No evidence found of an operator change; the project continues to be developed and would be operated by QPPL itself, per EGCO's own site.

Unchanged. EGCO's own 2026 corporate strategy release (POWER4) still references the Quezon Power Plant (Philippines) as part of its portfolio, consistent with continued full ownership. No re-sale or divestment reported.

Unchanged. Anchor year confirmed as 2024, the year QPPL filed its public-scoping/environmental-compliance documents with DENR (per the source-body reporting, February 2024), not a later publication date.
